one_line: Start with the parent's holiday problem as text and voice over the product already in kids' hands.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 extreme close-up of a beige fabric tunnel with a handwritten brand logo, a girl's hand pulling it; at 0:01 two girls in a garden. Voiceover (transcript) and subtitles: "תקופת החגים והחופשות שבה היא פשוט אתגר לכל אמא!".
q1_hook.why: A parent problem in text and voice from the first second, over busy movement (H1, H6, K6), with the product in children's hands at once (S1). The brand logo fills the first frame close up (H3, H7). No adult speaks to the camera, so the voice is brand-script (H4, H8).

beats.what: Brand logo close-up on a tunnel; two girls in a garden; "תקופת החגים והחופשות ... אתגר לכל אמא!"
A girl steps on round foam; a hand wipes a foam piece; "הג'ימבורי הביתי", "הסטפס"
beats.why: Names the product and a first benefit, easy cleaning

beats.what: Toddler and girls jump on steps by a play tent; text lists five pieces, foam fill, non-slip base
beats.why: A feature list while kids move

beats.what: Tent and tunnel join; a toddler crawls through, a view from inside the tunnel
beats.why: The play corner in use, a fresh POV

beats.what: A toddler jumps on the pieces; "הרכבה סופר קלה", "תיק נשיאה קומפקטי", "לשמור עליהם נקיים"
beats.why: Set-up and cleaning claims, said over play

beats.what: A hand and a girl walk past; a girl crawls to the lens; "אז למה אתן מחכות?"
beats.why: A rhetorical question and a site pointer

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None. "אז למה אתן מחכות?" is rhetorical. The caption is a personal statement with no question, and nothing to save or send beyond a gift-free product idea.
q2_flow.why: A new angle every 2 to 3 s and children always moving keep the Reel from sagging (R3, R1), and 27 s suits a single demo (R2). It is a feature list over play with no emotional peak, turn or payoff, and it stops on a call to visit a site (K2, K1, R4).

q3_cta.what: 0:24-0:27, voiced and subtitled: "אז למה אתן מחכות?" and "מגוון פרינטים מעלפים מחכים" (the transcript adds "לכם באתר"). Caption: no ask, no link or code, only the tag @bliss.il.
q3_cta.why: It is said and shown after the benefits (C6), but is a rhetorical question and a pointer with no link, code or named step, in the bottom third. The caption does not repeat it (C6). The viewer must find the site alone.

q4_shown.what: The brand logo on the tunnel 0:00; a girl on foam 0:03; a hand wiping a piece 0:05; a toddler and girls on steps by a play tent 0:07-0:13; a toddler in the tunnel 0:14-0:18; jumping 0:19-0:23. No set-up step, no price.
q4_shown.why: The product is in use from 0:00 (S1), and several children of different ages vouch by playing (K8). The wipe-clean shot answers one doubt (C7). Easy set-up is said but not shown, and there is no price (S3). Children's faces appear (S5).

q5_edit.what: 10 shots in 27.2 s, about 2.7 s each; hard cuts, handheld, with no speed changes. Subtitles in two lines synced to a voiceover that runs almost wall to wall. Text is white and thin. Ends on a POV from inside the tunnel.
q5_edit.why: A cut every 2 to 3 s and a change of angle keep a brisk pace (E2). Synced subtitles carry the voiceover muted (E4). It ends inside the tunnel, a fresh shot on the last line (E8). The thin type over bright footage is hard to read (T5).

q6_topic.what: A foam play set with a tent and tunnel as a way through school holidays, shown by children in a garden. Serves parents of several children looking for home activity.
q6_topic.why: The holiday problem is a real, seasonal concern (K6, K7), and the caption's "five children" line makes the speaker a peer. The tone is a brand script of features, not a story, so little invites a send (R5, K4).

q7_filmed.what: Handheld at child height in a garden with a pale play tent, daylight, mixed lighting from sun and shade; low angles on feet and steps; a POV from inside a fabric tunnel; one close-up of a hand wiping. No adult face.
q7_filmed.why: A home garden and daylight look native (H8, F7), and the POV inside the tunnel is a fresh view for the viewer (F5). Pieces are small in the wide frames (F4), and subtitles sit low over the children's legs (F2).

q8_text.on_screen: Thin white condensed subtitles with a light shadow, centred about 75% down, two lines at most, changing every 1 to 3 s: "תקופת החגים והחופשות שבה היא פשוט אתגר לכל אמא!" (0:01), "הג'ימבורי הביתי" (0:05), "הסטפס" (0:06), "הרכבה סופר קלה, נפתח בשניות" (0:19), "אז למה אתן מחכות?" (0:24). No headline card.
q8_text.caption: "אם רק היו מייצרים את הג׳ימבורי המושלם הזה כשהייתי עם ילד ראשון!!". Three short lines: a hook, a benefit line, then "פרסום בשיתוף עם המותג שאני הכי אוהבת @bliss.il". No hashtags, no CTA.
q8_text.why: Subtitles let a muted viewer follow (T1), but the type is thin and light over bright footage (T5, T2) in the bottom 35% (T4). The caption's first line is a real hook with the product named, but has no hashtags (T7), and the disclosure is in words, though last in the caption (T8, S7).

weak_points: Brand-script voiceover reading like an ad; thin, low-contrast subtitles over bright footage; no real CTA, link or code; disclosure only in the last caption line, none in the video; children's faces; set-up said, not shown.
lumebook_takeaway: Open with the parent's real problem as one text line over hands paging the book, add three short bold feature lines, end on one concrete ask.
not_verified: Whose voice it is (the creator's or not). The transcript mishears some words, so subtitle text was read from the frames. Whether set-up is shown in real time. The follower count. Music is not evident. The src/coded hook text matches the frames; no correction needed. Lead edit 18 Oct: resolution remarks removed, because the downloaded copy can be smaller than what was posted.
